title: Buy a thing, or buy time?
hook: Would you spend the same money on an item or on avoiding a chore?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Separate spending amount from the kind of benefit being purchased.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Separate spending amount from the kind of benefit being purchased.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A toy service costs €30 and frees sixty minutes valued at €1 each. What is its net value under that rule? Toy inputs A=[30, 60, 1]; B=[30, 0, 1].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[30, 60, 30], [-30, 0, 30]]. Labels: Net value €, Minutes freed, Price €.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: The price is held fixed while the kind of benefit changes. Valuing freed time is an explicit preference assumption in this model; another time value would change the conclusion. A purchase category alone does not guarantee higher satisfaction.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Price €=30, Minutes freed=0, €/minute=1. What is Net value €? Answer: -30.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Price €=30, Minutes freed=0, €/minute=1. What is Net value €?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives -30. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Paying for time-saving services raised life satisfaction more than buying goods (Whillans et al., 2017).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Separate spending amount from the kind of benefit being purchased.
